original.method: A private daemon (its own AGENTDOCKER_HOME, agentd.toml with [journal] retention = "120s") and a scratch checkout. Ten registered agents cycle claim (path lease with a note), release (with a summary, a journal entry each), send and ack between neighbours, a checkpoint every ten cycles and a journal read every 25 cycles from a cursor taken before the first prune. At half time five agents leave (their workers stop, then deregister). Every 60 seconds checkpoints older than 30 seconds are pruned. An event watcher counts journal_pruned (with reason) and checkpoints_pruned. Samples every ten seconds: daemon RSS, database bytes, journal rows, oldest retained entry, checkpoints, ping latency.

scenarios: retention pruned the journal 18 times by itself (11832 entries); the oldest retained entry is 121s old against a 120s window
a reader with a cursor from before the first prune read 500 pages in order; head_seq rose from 10 to 12622 and never fell
checkpoint pruning removed 420 checkpoints of the 5 finished agents and kept every one of the 5 live agents'
after retention took hold the database averaged 1.00x and the daemon's memory 0.98x of the middle third; journal rows 1549 -> 1084

assertions: retention pruned by itself (journal_pruned with reason retention) and the oldest retained entry never exceeded the window by more than 75 seconds (the minute tick plus batching)
a reader holding a cursor from before the first prune read pages in order and its head sequence never fell
finished agents' checkpoints older than 30 seconds were pruned while every live agent's were kept
database bytes and daemon RSS in the last third of the run stayed under 1.5x and 1.3x of the middle third, once prunes had been seen
vacuum after the run reclaimed space and the daemon log carried no warnings or errors
original.scope: Historical, original driver at 7937741: it asserted that some finished checkpoint was pruned (not every eligible one by id), compared journal heads against a value shared across reader threads, checked the oldest retained entry only at the end, and ran the daemon from the checkout's target directory. Kept as recorded; the rerun below asserts what this record claims.
